Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nimbus Cloud Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nimbus Cloud's results for the Q2 2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Hayes, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Morales, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Lee, Chief Product Officer; Sophia Grant, Chief Marketing Officer; Derek Wong, Chief Sales Officer; Nadia Patel, Chief Security Officer; and Dr. Liam Foster, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nimbus Cloud delivered exceptional results for the Q2, demonstrating the strength of our cloud platform and the increasing demand for our AI-driven solutions across diverse industries.

During the quarter, we focused on eight key strategic priorities:
1. Expanding our global reach through strategic partnerships.
2. Driving innovation in edge computing and IoT solutions.
3. Enhancing our commitment to open source technologies.
4. Strengthening our data privacy and compliance programs.
5. Investing in our employees' professional development.
6. Improving our operational efficiency through automation.
7. Fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.
8. Accelerating the adoption of sustainable cloud practices.

Let me dive into our progress on sustainability, which has become a cornerstone of how we operate and compete. In the cloud industry, data centers consume about 2-3% of global electricity, expected to reach 1,000 TWh annually by 2026 according to the IEA. Sustainability drives our margins, keeps customers loyal, and ensures compliance. With workloads up over 45% year-over-year in AI and gen AI, we've outperformed peers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

Our fleet-wide Power Usage Effectiveness hit 1.10 in Q2, improving 15% from 1.29 at the end of last year and beating the 1.20 hyperscaler average from Uptime Institute's survey. This saved us $285 million annually in energy costs, adding 120 basis points to our non-GAAP operating margin. Water Usage Effectiveness improved 22% to 0.18 liters per kWh via closed-loop cooling.

On renewables, we matched 85% of consumption, up from 72% last year, through 15-year power purchase agreements for solar in Texas and Arizona, offshore wind in the Nordics, and hydro in Quebec. We're on pace for 100% by end-2025, ahead of some peers. Scope 1 and 2 emissions fell 28% to 1.2 million metric tons CO2e, and we're starting Scope 3 reporting at 4.5 million tons, targeting 12% reduction next year with our Cloud Carbon Footprint Tool in 60% of enterprise dashboards.

Technically, our custom silicon rollout has 40% of instances on Nimbus Graviton4 ARM processors, 25% more efficient per core-hour than x86, with 0.35 joules per TOPS for inference. Our AutoScaler AI uses reinforcement learning to right-size clusters, cutting idle power 32% and saving 1.2 billion kWh in Q2—enough for 120,000 US homes. Immersion cooling in 15% of facilities reduced cooling energy 45%, with pilots under 1.05 PUE in Virginia and Frankfurt.

Regionally, North America at 92% renewables and 1.08 PUE; Europe at 95% with wind in Ireland; APAC at 78% in Singapore and Tokyo, investing $500 million in Osaka tidal; emerging markets with solar microgrids in India and Brazil for 5G.

Customers love it—68% of top 100 deals have ESG clauses, up from 42%, boosting NPS 14 points. Energy efficiency added $420 million to H1 free cash flow. We're committing $2.8 billion CapEx this year for liquid-cooled campuses and 2 GW wind, targeting net-zero by 2030 with photonic interconnects and carbon-aware scheduling. This generates real alpha as ESG funds eye cloud infra.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hayes to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Alex. We are very pleased with our financial results for the Q2. Revenue increased by 28% year-over-year to $7.2 billion, exceeding our guidance for the quarter. Our gross margin was 73.2%, driven by our efficient cost management and economies of scale. Our operating margin was 32%.

Let me discuss our pricing strategies and discounting, key to growth in this hyperscale market against AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Pricing drives acquisition, usage, retention, and margins amid AI/ML surges and macro pressures.

Our core model is consumption-based for IaaS, PaaS, SaaS like Nimbus Compute, Nebula Storage, Apex AI. Optimizations include Arm64 instances at 40% better price-performance. Blends: on-demand at $0.046/vCPU-hour; Reserved Instances and Savings Plans at 30-60% off—RI adoption 55%, up from 48%; Spot at 90% off for 15% of batch AI.

This lifted ARPU 12% to $142K, but blended discount rate rose to 22% from 18% to match Azure bundles and Google funds. 40% of 32% cloud growth from elasticity—35% compute hours surge, AI/ML now 28% revenue with 22% usage uplift per 10% discount.

Net new ACV $1.8B up 25%, trials-to-paid 65% vs. Gartner 52%; churn 4.2%. Margins compressed 120bps, 60bps from discounts, but op margin held via supply efficiencies.

Key metrics: discount rate +4pts to 22%; compute +35% (40% from discounts); RI mix +7pts to 55%; gross 73.2% (-120bps, -60 from discounts); AI % +10pts.

Tools like Nimbus Price Optimizer save 25-35%, 70% adoption; Apex Accelerate 50% off GPUs; 10% sustainability discounts. Regions: NA 18% discounts, 55% rev; EMEA 20%, +42% growth; APAC 28%, India +55%; ROW +60% LatAm.

Competitively, our Arm/GPU edge and pay-per-query pilots shine. Q3 discounts 23%, 30% growth, margins to 74%.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Morales, who will provide an update on our technology strategy and roadmap.

Dr. Elena Morales:
Thank you, Jordan. We are committed to leading the way in cloud technology innovation. We are making significant investments in research and development to create cutting-edge solutions for our customers.

Today, I'll cover our investments in security infrastructure and personnel, vital amid AI phishing, supply chain attacks, and ransomware. We spent $450 million in Q2, 22% of $2.05B CapEx, up 35% YoY; TTM $1.7B up from $1.2B. 60% infrastructure, 40% people. MTTD/MTTR improved 42%/31%; 99.999% uptime.

Infrastructure: confidential computing with SGX/SEV-SNP, 500K instances +150% QoQ for finance/healthcare. Post-quantum crypto Kyber/Dilithium in KMS, EOY 2025 target. Zero-trust with Istio/Envoy/eBPF, 55% risk reduction; new SOCs in Singapore, Sao Paulo, Dublin—12 total, AI SIEM 15PB/day.

Personnel: security team to 4,200 FTEs +28%, $180M with 12% comp rise, $50M academy, 92% retention.

Regions: EMEA $144M GDPR zones; APAC $110M interconnects +50% FS workloads; Americas $196M threat intel.

This builds moat, Gartner $75B market 17% CAGR; integrated stack 30% better TCO, NPS 78, 15 Fortune 500 wins. Q4 $500M, Nimbus Shield AI automates 70% triage; EBITDA to 36% FY26.

Now, I'll pass it over to Marcus Lee to discuss our product roadmap and recent launches.

Marcus Lee:
Thank you, Dr. Morales. We recently launched NimbusForge, a groundbreaking solution designed to revolutionize AI inference workloads.

I'll focus on overall gross margin trends and drivers, showing our scalable infra and mix shift. Q2 gross margin 72.5%, +150bps YoY, +80bps QoQ—11th straight expansion.

Mix: IaaS 42% rev down from 48%, +28% growth; PaaS/SaaS higher, AI/ML 82% margins 15% rev +6pts; Kubernetes 78% +45%.

Costs: power/cooling -12%/rack liquid cooling/renewables 65%, -$120M QoQ; depr/amort -9% 92% util Fabric networking.

Custom silicon 60% inference, -35% GPU dep +200bps. Regions: NA 74%; EMEA +250bps 71%; APAC 69%; LATAM 67% +55% growth.

Q4 guide 73-74%, AI/PaaS 20%+, Nitro enclaves. Hedged 85% risks.

I'll now hand it over to Sophia Grant to provide an update on our marketing initiatives and brand strategy.

Sophia Grant:
Thank you, Marcus. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and driving demand for our innovative solutions.

Let me share our new customer acquisition cost analysis, core to efficiency. CAC $42,300/new customer, -12% YoY from $48,100, -5% QoQ. Enterprise $78,200 -15%; SMB $8,400, free tier 28% conversion +6pts.

Marketing CAC $15,200 -18%, AI lead scoring 3x MQLs, payback 6.5 months. Sales $27,100 -9%, 45% partners 5-8% rev-share.

Regions: NA $38,900, 92-day cycles; EMEA $52,400 +4% QoQ; APAC $36,700 -20%. LTV/CAC 4.8x, payback 11.2 months, NRR 118%.

Ahead: Zero-Touch beta -25% SMB CAC, $150M partners to 55% indirect. FY24 <$40k, Rule of 40 68%.

Next, I'd like to introduce Derek Wong, who will discuss our sales performance and customer acquisition strategies.

Derek Wong:
Thank you, Sophia. Our sales team has been instrumental in driving our strong growth in the Q2. We are focused on expanding our customer base and strengthening our existing relationships.

On churn and retention, annualized dollar churn 6.8% -140bps YoY, GRR 94.5% +140bps. NRR 119% +300bps, existing base +19%.

Cohorts: FY22 128%, FY23 115%, new 105%. Enterprise 125% +4pts ARR share; mid 112%; SMB 108%.

Drivers: KubeEngine -40% deploys; FinOps 25-30% savings; Inference Engine 3x adoption $450K ARR; sovereignty.

Regions: NA 122% sub-5% churn; EMEA 114%; APAC 110%; ROW 108%. CS NPS 68 +6. Q4 churn <6.5%, NRR 121%, 65% multi-year.

Now, I'll pass it over to Nadia Patel to discuss our security initiatives and commitment to data protection.

Nadia Patel:
Thank you, Derek. Security is paramount to our mission. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and ensuring the integrity of our cloud platform.

IaaS $4.6-4.7B +24-26%, CF-GPU300 40% better perf, storage $1.05B +18% zero-egress. PaaS $2B-2.05B +17-19%, AuroraDB +28%, VectorForge $450M ARR. Other $0.85-0.86B flat.

Regions: Americas $4.9-4.95B +23% AI 28%; EMEA $1.5-1.525B +19% sovereign; APAC $1.1-1.125B +18%.

FY24 $29-29.5B +20-21%. Op margin 32-32.5% Q3, 33.5% FY; FCF $8.75-9.25B.

Drivers: AI $3.75B +60%, Nebula supercluster; multi-cloud Arc/Anthos; sustainability.

Risks GPU supply, upside genAI.

Finally, I'd like to introduce Dr. Liam Foster, who will share insights into our innovation strategy and future growth opportunities.

Dr. Liam Foster:
Thank you, Nadia. We are constantly exploring new technologies and business models to drive innovation and create value for our customers.

Our CapEx outlook reflects commitment to hyperscale leadership. Q2 $4.8B in line +18% YoY, 500MW new capacity GPU clusters.

FY24 raised to $22-24B +25-28%; Q4 $6-6.5B; FY25 $24-27B. Categories: data centers 55-60% $12-14B, 1.2GW adds Virginia/Frankfurt/Singapore, 40% liquid GPU, NA50% EMEA25% APAC25%.

AI/ML 25-30% $5.5-7B, NIE-2 2.5x tokens/dollar, 60% inference. Networking/storage/sust 10-15% $2.5-3.5B 800Gbps, 11 9's, PUE<1.2 100% renewable.

Pillars: AI 35% $100B market; efficiency -25% intensity; resilience sovereign $2B. 28-30% rev, 85% util.

Back to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term sustainable growth.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On pricing and discounting, with discounts up to 22%, how do you balance growth versus margin pressure going into Q3?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, John. Our pricing is dynamic to stimulate usage, especially AI, where elasticity is high. We've seen 35% compute growth from it, and with RI mix at 55%, revenue is predictable. Margins dipped but rebound to 74% in Q3 as utilization rises. It's strategic, not a race to bottom.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Thanks. On the revenue guidance raise to $29-29.5B FY24, what gives you confidence amid macro uncertainty, and any segment color?

Jordan Hayes:
Emily, thanks. Strong RPO $42B +28%, 95% visibility. AI tailwinds huge, IaaS +24% Q3 on GPUs, PaaS on databases/vector DBs. Regions balanced, sovereign bright. We've baked in FX and supply risks, but NRR 119% supports acceleration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good afternoon. For innovation, how are sustainability initiatives impacting new opportunities like edge AI?

Dr. Liam Foster:
David, sustainability opens doors—68% enterprise deals have ESG, NPS up 14. PUE 1.10 enables efficient edge with solar microgrids in India/Brazil, low latency 5G. $2.8B CapEx funds green campuses, positioning for ESG funds and regs like EU CSRD.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Wong:
Thanks. On security investments, with $450M spend, what's the ROI in terms of customer wins and MTTD improvements?

Dr. Elena Morales:
Sarah, ROI clear: MTTD/MTTR -42%/-31%, 99.999% uptime. 15 Fortune 500 wins, hyperscaler defection on confidential compute. TCO 30% better, scales with $75B market. Nimbus Shield AI next for automation.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions and your continued interest in Nimbus Cloud.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
